intro.title: Introduction
intro.summary: To judge whether a work on a cosmic scale could exist, you must first understand what it would take to last. Matter, energy, heat and time will be the limits that accompany the entire journey.

visualization.caption: Scales chained from a ship to a technologically active galaxy.

visual.visualFocus: A load module takes off from the Moon, with the Earth and an orbital habitat on the horizon.

intro.question: What does it mean to build on a cosmic scale?

habitats.title: Space habitats
habitats.summary: Inhabiting space requires converting basic needs into reliable systems. Understanding how air, water and protection are sustained is the basis for imagining any artificial world.

sections.title: A home needs protection and maintenance
sections.body: The shape of the habitat is not enough. Its envelope should conserve air, limit exposure to radiation and protect against impacts. Filters, pumps and structures need inspection and repair: closing the water cycle does not eliminate the need for spare parts.

visualization.caption: Revolving habitats compared by scale, comfort and material difficulty.
visualization.fallback: torus, sphere and cylinder rotating to simulate gravity.

visual.visualFocus: A monumental orbital habitat of habitable rings and modules connected to a central axis.

habitats.question: What does an artificial world need to remain habitable?

infrastructure.title: Space infrastructure
infrastructure.summary: Large space works depend on a previous transport, material and manufacturing network. Understanding that network shows how isolated missions could become a permanent capacity to build away from Earth.

sections.title: Being close doesn't mean sharing an orbit.
sections.body: An orbit is a path of falling around a body. To find a port it is not enough to reach its height: you have to adjust trajectory and speed. Fuel, tanks and systems that exchange movement convert points of space into a transport network.

visualization.caption: Nodes, routes and megastructures connecting surface, orbit, moon and asteroids.
visualization.fallback: Orbital network with ports, depots, tethers and rings.

visual.visualFocus: Ports, warehouses, shipyards, orbital load and space logistics as an industrial network.

infrastructure.question: Where do materials and machines come from?

planetary.title: Planetary engineering
planetary.summary: Changing a planet affects its environments and, perhaps, the life that already exists. Comparing local shelters and terraforming allows measuring what would be needed, how long it would take and what consequences it would have.

visualization.caption: Planetary laboratory with atmospheres, mirrors, parasols, domes and magnetospheres.
visualization.fallback: Planet with modifiable layers of atmosphere, energy and protection.

visual.visualFocus: Mars, domes, atmospheric processors, orbital mirrors and partial habitability.

planetary.question: Adapt to a world or modify it?

groups.title: Intervention on light, atmosphere and materials

propulsion.title: Interstellar travel
propulsion.summary: The possibility of reaching another star depends on solving the entire journey. That means choosing how to speed up, keep the ship safe during the crossing and slow down on arrival.

sections.title: Accelerating is just a part of the journey
sections.body: The thrust changes the movement of a ship by ejecting matter or interacting with something external, like a beam of light. Having a lot of energy does not guarantee a great thrust. Getting to another system also requires reducing speed: the design of the trip must include this braking from the beginning.

visualization.caption: Map of propulsion technologies from current rockets to relativistic border.
visualization.fallback: Engine fan ordered by thrust, efficiency and maturity.

visual.visualFocus: Interstellar ship over an icy landscape before a ringed giant and a starry sky.

propulsion.question: How to get there, stop and survive the journey?

energy.title: Stellar energy
energy.summary: Every large-scale work needs energy at its height. Catching starlight is only the beginning: transporting it and dissipating heat determine whether that energy can be used.

visualization.caption: From solar satellites to Dyson swarms and waste heat detectable.
visualization.fallback: Star surrounded by collectors and radiators.

visual.visualFocus: Reflective stellar scale panels under the light of a star, with a close-up maintenance robot.

energy.question: How do you capture so much energy without getting caught up in your heat?

search.title: Alien intelligence
search.summary: After imagining what other civilizations might build, one wonders what traces they would leave. Searching for signals and technosignatures turns that possibility into an investigation and requires a careful interpretation of silence.

visualization.caption: Compared civilizations for energy, detectability, expansion and silence.
visualization.fallback: Galaxy with slow routes, technosignatures and silent regions.

visual.visualFocus: technosignatures, SETI, subtle galactic structures and the question of cosmic silence.

search.question: How would we recognize those who have already done so?

civilizations.title: Cosmic civilizations
civilizations.summary: Technologies capable of transforming worlds would also transform those who use them. Energy, computing and expansion help you think about what forms of civilization might arise on a cosmic scale.

visualization.caption: Compared civilizations for energy, detectability, expansion and silence.
visualization.fallback: Galaxy with slow routes, technosignatures and silent regions.

visual.visualFocus: technosignatures, SETI, subtle galactic structures and the question of cosmic silence.

civilizations.question: What could become of a civilization capable of building on a cosmic scale?

groups.title: Computerization and other forms of existence

stellar.title: Stellar engineering
stellar.summary: Intervention by a star would test our limits of energy, time and control. Exploring how to move it, extract its matter or alter its evolution allows us to measure how far physical laws could take us.

visualization.caption: Star engines, plasma extraction and slow movement of solar systems.
visualization.fallback: Star with mirror, collectors and plasma jets.

visual.visualFocus: A colossal structure next to a star, with planets and an engineering base on the lunar surface.

stellar.question: Can a star become an engineering object?

astroingenieria.title: Astroengineering
astroingenieria.summary: Engineering imagined or studied at spatial, planetary, stellar and galactic scales.
astroingenieria.keyIdea: It is not just building ships: it is thinking about what a civilization can build when it dominates energy, materials and deep time.
astroingenieria.mentalImage: A ladder that starts in an orbital station and ends up in a galaxy full of visible infrastructure.
astroingenieria.mechanism: It unites physics, astronomy, engineering, habitability, energy, space politics and hard science fiction on a map of possibilities.
advantages: Order huge ideas on understandable scales
Connect real technology with speculative boundaries
difficulties: Many proposals depend on materials and economies that are not yet available
It is easy to mix plausibility with spectacle

iss.summary: Orbital laboratories such as ISS and Tiangong show life support, microgravity, maintenance and real space cooperation.
iss.keyIdea: They are the first practical step before thinking of giant rotating colonies.

advantages: Continuous learning about life outside the Earth
difficulties: Depending on resupply and intensive maintenance

artificial-gravity.title: Artificial gravity through rotation

artificial-gravity.keyIdea: The size allows to turn slower and reduce dizziness by Coriolis.
artificial-gravity.mentalImage: People walking through the inside of a ring that slowly rotates around a luminous axis.
artificial-gravity.mechanism: Centripetal acceleration holds the inhabitants against the interior floor; radius and angular velocity define comfort.
advantages: Allows interior worlds with stable architecture
difficulties: Small radios generate uncomfortable sensory effects
